headline_results.compression: INT8 remained the strongest Phase 1 compression result; TT/MPS was implemented and evaluated without establishing superiority.
headline_results.cross_domain: A shared computational framework was demonstrated at the framework and interface level, not as one universal trained policy.
headline_results.lyapunov: Hard action/domain guards dominated observed interventions in several regimes. Lyapunov-specific candidate selection became active under action perturbation in driving but not robotics.
headline_results.rl_qml: Classical PPO reached 6/6 frozen targets, matched classical reached 1/6, and hybrid QML reached 0/6. The hybrid actor nevertheless demonstrated substantial parameter compactness.
headline_results.safety: Explicit safety filtering produced strong empirical pilot effects across both domains, with robustness evaluated under Gaussian, structured-state, and action perturbations.
headline_results.training_efficiency: No robust >=10% training-efficiency improvement was demonstrated under the frozen protocol.

limitations.statement: The shared Phase 1 VLA baseline is compact and does not represent a production-scale pretrained VLA backbone.
Sprint 4 RL policies consume compact environment state rather than the Sprint 1 shared VLA latent representation.
The principal trained-policy protocol uses three seeds.
Safety evaluations use 20 held-out episodes per seed/condition in the principal protocol.
The Phase 1 hybrid QML pathway uses a small simulated 4-qubit, 2-layer PQC.
No quantum hardware execution was performed.
TT/MPS compression was evaluated at pilot-model scale.
No principal CARLA, nuScenes, or physical-vehicle evaluation was performed.
No principal RLBench, LIBERO, Open X-Embodiment, or physical-robot evaluation was performed.
During perception-perturbation experiments, the policy used perturbed/noisy observations while the safety layer retained access to true simulator state.
Environment action-bound handling is accounted for separately from explicit safety-filter intervention.
The implemented Lyapunov quantity is an empirical safety potential and does not constitute a formal closed-loop stability proof.
No functional-safety certification or standards compliance is claimed.
No production deployment or full-scale embedded VLA validation was performed.

lyapunov_nuance.canonical_statement: Hard action/domain guards accounted for the observed interventions in clean, Gaussian, and structured-state regimes. Lyapunov-specific candidate selection became empirically active under action perturbation, with activation observed in autonomous driving but not robotics.

phase2_roadmap.phase1_gap_addressed: Sprint 4 policies operated on compact environment state rather than the Sprint 1 shared latent.

phase2_roadmap.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 tensor-network experiments were limited to the compact pilot architecture.

phase2_roadmap.objective: Move from synthetic proxy environments to realistic driving and robotics benchmarks.
phase2_roadmap.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 validation used synthetic proxy environments.

phase2_roadmap.objective: Evaluate safety filters when both policy and safety layer receive estimated or noisy state.
phase2_roadmap.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 perception-perturbation studies allowed the safety layer access to true simulator state.

phase2_roadmap.objective: Measure end-to-end latency, memory, and safety-filter overhead on embedded hardware.

phase2_roadmap.objective: Increase statistical strength and broaden evaluation.
phase2_roadmap.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 used three principal seeds and compact evaluation settings.

architecture.allowed_summary: Cross-domain reuse is supported at the framework and interface level, not as one universal trained policy.

compression.allowed_summary: INT8 remained the strongest Phase 1 compression result; TT/MPS provided an implemented quantum-inspired pathway without demonstrating superiority.

rl_qml.allowed_summary: Classical PPO reached all frozen targets. The hybrid PQC actor was substantially more compact but did not demonstrate sample-efficiency advantage.

safety.allowed_summary: Explicit safety filtering produced strong empirical pilot effects. Robustness was evaluated across Gaussian, structured-state, and action perturbations. Lyapunov-specific mechanism activation remained domain-dependent.

training_efficiency.allowed_summary: No robust >=10% training-efficiency improvement was demonstrated under the frozen Phase 1 protocol.

sprint6_status_statement: The original Sprint 6 implementation cycle was not executed. Its proposal-critical architecture-integration and Phase 2 planning requirements were captured through Sprint 5.14.5. Larger end-to-end integration experiments are deferred to Phase 2.

supported_claims.statement: A shared computational framework was instantiated across autonomous-driving and robotics proxy domains.
All four Volkswagen challenge bottlenecks were experimentally addressed in the Phase 1 pilot.
INT8 satisfied the strongest Phase 1 compression criterion under the frozen pilot configuration.
The hybrid PQC policy actor demonstrated substantial parameter compactness in both domains.
Explicit clean safety filtering was empirically effective under the frozen driving and robotics proxy contracts.
Gaussian observation robustness was evaluated under the frozen Phase 1 protocol.
Structured-state robustness was evaluated under domain-specific perturbation contracts.
Action perturbation robustness and unsafe-action recovery were quantified.
Cross-domain safety-framework reuse was demonstrated at the framework and interface level.

supported_with_limitation.limitation: The scale-up itself has not yet been experimentally demonstrated.
supported_with_limitation.statement: The Phase 1 architecture provides a modular Phase 2 scale-up pathway.

supported_with_limitation.limitation: Observed interventions were often dominated by hard action/domain guards, and Lyapunov-specific activation was domain-dependent.
supported_with_limitation.statement: Lyapunov-guided safety was empirically effective under the frozen pilot safety contract.

supported_with_limitation.limitation: The perturbation studies used synthetic proxy environments and do not establish real-world robustness.
supported_with_limitation.statement: Robustness was demonstrated under synthetic Gaussian, structured-state, and action perturbations.

unsupported_claims.statement: Hybrid QML demonstrated sample-efficiency superiority over classical PPO.
TT/MPS demonstrated compression superiority over the strongest classical baseline.
A robust training-efficiency advantage was demonstrated.
A universal trained VLA policy was demonstrated across driving and robotics.
Zero-shot cross-domain policy transfer was demonstrated.
Formal Lyapunov closed-loop stability was demonstrated.
A formal safety guarantee was demonstrated.
Production safety or deployment readiness was demonstrated.
Safety certification or standards compliance was demonstrated.
